messages:
ashley: @here Observed a major latency spike affecting Vertex Labs (dedicated VPC pool) in eu-west-1. p95 climbed from ~120ms to ~2.1s and p99 to ~3.8s starting ~2026-03-14T10:12Z. Dashboard: per-route token latency + queue depth high for pool-dedicated-eu-west-vertex. incident-bot: created INC-2026-042 (severity 2)

incident-bot: Paging oncall (ashley) for INC-2026-042 - High latency, customer-impacting. Notify: platform, eng-sre, customer-success.

ashley: Quick checks — control plane shows many inflight requests on the pool. Worker oom/evictions? Not seeing node crashes. Throughput (tokens/s) steady, but queue wait increasing.

miguel: On it. Attaching a quick metric snippet: `p95: 2100ms, p99: 3800ms, queue_depth: 180` for pool-dedicated-eu-west-vertex.

ashley: Vertex CS says they started seeing user complaints at ~10:12Z. Etta, can you confirm tenant priority and business impact?

etta: Vertex (enterprise) confirms customer-impacting: web UI timeouts, several API calls failing after 10s. They're on Dedicated with VPC peering. Escalating to their infra lead.

jordan: Suggestion: traffic routing shows we have a failover warm pool in eu-west-2 and us-east-1. Two options: 1) divert Vertex traffic to warm pool in eu-west-2; 2) enable model-variant fallback to quantized variant (redwood-quant-v1) for Vertex to reduce per-token CPU/latency. Need quick consensus.

ashley: Can we do both? Apply fallback first (low-risk) and prepare routing change if not sufficient.

miguel: I'll trigger model-variant fallback to 20% canary and monitor. Command: ```rwdctl routing update --tenant vertex-labs --policy fallback --variant redwood-quant-v1 --sample 0.2``` Executed at 10:22Z.

dave: I'm watching infra. Node CPU on the pool jumped to 95% across several servers; some RPC queue backpressure. Checking kernel threads and netstats. No OOMs yet.

vertex-cs (customer): Confirmed — we see slight improvement for a subset of calls; but overall still bad, p99 still >3s.

miguel: Canary shows p95 improved to ~550ms for the 20% traffic slice, p99 for that slice ~850ms. So variant helps. For full mitigation we either increase fallback to 100% or shift region.

ashley: For safety, increase fallback to 60% now. If stable, we'll flip to 100% then consider rolling capacity change.

miguel: Increasing to 60%: ```rwdctl routing update --tenant vertex-labs --policy fallback --variant redwood-quant-v1 --sample 0.6``` Done at 10:31Z. Monitoring...

jordan: Start preparing region failover play: pre-warm eu-west-2 pool and update routing policy to route Vertex to eu-west-2. Note: VPC peering and private endpoints require reconfiguration — coordinate with Vertex network team (etta).

etta: I'm on Vertex call now, asking them to be ready to accept a routed endpoint change. They can update peering but will need ~10-15min.

dave: Meanwhile, I see several connections from a single client IP pattern causing high cost per request. Possibly a noisy worker on Vertex side or a bad client loop. I can rate-limit at the reverse proxy for that tenant. Do we want to throttle?

ashley: Yes, apply a soft throttle (50 req/s) to that client-id for 5 minutes and observe. Command: ```rwdctl quota update --tenant vertex-labs --target client:12345 --rate 50/s --duration 5m```

miguel: Throttle applied at 10:36Z. The overall queue length started to drop. p95 of the remaining non-fallback traffic dropped to ~420ms.

vertex-cs (customer): We're seeing improvement, still intermittent spikes but user complaints decreased.

oncall-l7: Recommend we also evict KV/prefix cache for Vertex — cache misses could be amplifying token cost. To be careful: `rwdctl cache invalidate --tenant vertex-labs --prefix /chat/sessions` (low-risk).

jordan: Doing a safe cache invalidate on session prefixes now. Executed at 10:41Z.

miguel: After caches invalidated and 60% fallback + client throttle, p95 is ~210ms, p99 ~650ms for the full tenant. Queue depth back to normal. Still watching tail latencies on long-running seqs.

ashley: Nice work. Let's keep Vertex on 60% fallback for now and not flip to 100% until we see sustained 15m of stability. Also continue to prepare region failover plan in case.

etta: Vertex confirms they can do peering change but ask to avoid full region switch unless necessary. Their compliance team wants logs retained for the incident.

deploy-bot: Notifying: there is a scheduled infra scale-up in eu-west-1 in 20m (auto-scale policy). Consider accelerating if needed.

dave: I can bump dedicated pool capacity manually — estimate 2x nodes will remove CPU pressure, but scaling takes 8-12min to be fully healthy. Shall I initiate?

ashley: Go for it. Initiate 2x add now and keep monitoring. Document the exact action for postmortem.

dave: `rwdctl pool scale --name pool-dedicated-eu-west-vertex --replicas +2` executed at 10:47Z. Nodes provisioning.

miguel: Observability note: capture a quick flamegraph/stack samples on busy workers before scaling completes: `rd-agent prof --pool pool-dedicated-eu-west-vertex --duration 30s --out /tmp/vertex-profile.pb`

ashley: I'm going to hand off to miguel for the next 30m while I stay on the Vertex call for CS context. miguel, you're primary. I'll update the incident channel with any customer notes.

miguel: Acknowledged. I'll keep the lead, will escalate to platform if scaling or failover needed.

etta: Vertex reporting significant reduction in UI timeouts. They're marking impact as "degraded" rather than "outage" now.

ashley: Good. For incident record: action list so far: 1) Canary fallback to quantized variant (20% -> 60%), 2) soft throttle for noisy client, 3) cache invalidate, 4) manual pool scale +2, 5) monitoring & profile capture.

miguel: At 10:58Z nodes are healthy and CPU falling to ~60%. p95 stabilized ~180-220ms, p99 ~420ms. I'll keep 60% fallback for another 30m and then ramp down to measure.

vertex-cs (customer): Thank you — we see normalcy returning. We'll keep monitoring and notify if any regressions.

ashley: We'll run a postmortem. Please collect: pool logs, profile, routing changes, throttle events, and customer timeline. I'll file INC-2026-042 and assign owners.

incidents-bot: Incident INC-2026-042 updated: status -> monitoring, severity -> 2. Links: /incidents/INC-2026-042.

jordan: Quick note for postmortem: check whether prefix cache TTLs or KV eviction policy caused amplification after quantized fallback (we saw different cache behavior).

miguel: Will take ownership of postmortem write-up. Putting action items in issue tracker.

ashley: Thanks all. I'll update oncall rotation notes and hand back after Vertex call.

etta: Closing loop with Vertex: they appreciate the mitigation and ask to be informed before rollback of fallback.

miguel: Last check at 11:10Z: p95 190ms, p99 460ms. Leaving fallback at 60% until 11:40Z then we'll test ramp-down.

ashley: Sounds good. End of urgent ops for now.
